evidence_level: primary-literature follow-up audit, not a forecast outcome or executed experiment
frozen_question: Can an in-database functional-dependency table be kept correct under base-table updates with lower update-plus-query cost than re-mining the dependencies after every update?

pre_cutoff_prior_art.title: DynFD: Functional Dependency Discovery in Dynamic Datasets
pre_cutoff_prior_art.locator: PDF pp. 1-2, abstract and section 1; section 6 for evaluation
pre_cutoff_prior_art.verified_scope: Exact minimal FDs are maintained across inserts, updates and deletes. The paper compares incremental maintenance with repeated static discovery and reports an order-of-magnitude advantage in its evaluated setting.
pre_cutoff_prior_art.limit: This predates the frozen cutoff and therefore cannot be a future outcome. It does not by itself establish the source vision's in-database, user-queryable FD table with a matched update-plus-query workload. Re-mining alone is a weak novelty baseline because DynFD already existed.

in_window_near_match.title: Workload-driven, Lazy Discovery of Data Dependencies for Query Optimization
in_window_near_match.locator: PDF pp. 1-2 introduction/contributions; p. 4 section 3.2; pp. 5-6 sections 4.1-4.3 and Table 1
in_window_near_match.verified_scope: A Hyrise prototype discovers UCC, FD and OD metadata for query optimization. Section 3.2 proposes reuse of prior incremental FD maintenance approaches. The reported JOB improvement is 27% in query execution time after discovery.
in_window_near_match.mismatch: Section 4.1 measures query workload before and after invoking discovery separately, not a matched base-table-update plus FD-table-query trace versus repeated re-mining. It does not authenticate a user-queryable FD table with correct answers through updates under the frozen test. A design discussion of incremental maintenance is not a measured joint-cost result.

premise_revision_note: The generic premise that incremental FD maintenance remained unsolved in 2020 is contradicted by pre-cutoff DynFD. This narrows plausible novelty but is not a direct future refutation label under the frozen protocol.
next_check: Search for dated in-window primary implementations of a queryable in-database FD table with correctness under insert/update/delete and measured joint update-plus-query costs; compare any candidate with both static re-mining and the pre-cutoff DynFD baseline. Keep the frozen question unchanged.
